docs/spec-001-feature/review-development-project-manager.md

- Header: reviewer role (Development Project Manager), date 2026-10-27, inputs reviewed
- Findings table: ID, dimension (Coverage/Sequencing/Dependencies/Scope), severity (Critical/Warning/Suggestion), finding, suggested fix
- Per-dimension verdicts (Pass / Pass with notes / Fail)
- Overall verdict: APPROVED / APPROVED WITH NOTES / NEEDS REVISION
- An explicit "Gaps identified" section listing each gap and the suggested fix

Rules: DO NOT modify any file other than that review file. DO NOT change the plan/tasks/spec yourself — you only identify gaps and suggest fixes; the orchestrator resolves them. Be specific and evidence-based (cite the task/requirement IDs you checked). If everything is fine in a dimension, say so explicitly with what you verified. Keep the report tight and actionable.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 600000ms / 10 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

1	# wordstat: Interface Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, standard library only; pytest for tests only.
6	- **Package location:** `wordstat/` at repo root (flat layout, no `src/`).
7	- **Entry point:** `python -m wordstat ...` run from repo root.
8	
9	## Functional requirements
10	
11	- **R1** `python -m wordstat --help` exits 0.
12	- **R2** `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE` reads exactly one file, decoded as UTF-8 with an optional BOM (`utf-8-sig`). stdin is never read.
13	- **R3** Counts, computed on the decoded text:
14	  - `lines` = `len(text.splitlines())`
15	  - `words` = number of matches of `[a-z0-9]+` in `text.lower()`
16	  - `chars` = `len(text)` (code points, BOM excluded)
17	- **R4** `top` lists the `N` most frequent words (same tokens as R3), ordered by count descending, then word ascending. `--top` defaults to 3. Fewer than `N` distinct words lists all of them.
18	- **R5** Default output is the text format; `--json` selects the JSON format.
19	- **R6** Output is deterministic: UTF-8, `\n` line endings, no locale use. stdout is reconfigured to `encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"`.
20	
21	## Interface contract
22	
23	### Command
24	
25	```
26	python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE
27	```
28	
29	- argparse `prog` is `wordstat`.
30	- `--top` must be an integer >= 1, else usage error.
31	
32	### Text format
33	
34	Exactly four lines, each ending in `\n`:
35	
36	```
37	lines: <lines>
38	words: <words>
39	chars: <chars>
40	top: <word>=<count> <word>=<count> ...
41	```
42	
43	With no words, the last line is `top:` with no trailing space.
44	
45	### JSON format
46	
47	One line: the result of `json.dumps(obj)` with default separators, followed by `\n`, where `obj` has keys in this order:
48	
49	```

You are an agent for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. Given the user's message, you should use the tools available to complete the task. Complete the task fully—don't gold-plate, but don't leave it half-done. - Analyzing multiple files to understand system architecture
- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 600000ms / 10 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

1	# wordstat: Interface Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, standard library only; pytest for tests only.
6	- **Package location:** `wordstat/` at repo root (flat layout, no `src/`).
7	- **Entry point:** `python -m wordstat ...` run from repo root.
8	
9	## Functional requirements
10	
11	- **R1** `python -m wordstat --help` exits 0.
12	- **R2** `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE` reads exactly one file, decoded as UTF-8 with an optional BOM (`utf-8-sig`). stdin is never read.
13	- **R3** Counts, computed on the decoded text:
14	  - `lines` = `len(text.splitlines())`
15	  - `words` = number of matches of `[a-z0-9]+` in `text.lower()`
16	  - `chars` = `len(text)` (code points, BOM excluded)
17	- **R4** `top` lists the `N` most frequent words (same tokens as R3), ordered by count descending, then word ascending. `--top` defaults to 3. Fewer than `N` distinct words lists all of them.
18	- **R5** Default output is the text format; `--json` selects the JSON format.
19	- **R6** Output is deterministic: UTF-8, `\n` line endings, no locale use. stdout is reconfigured to `encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"`.
20	
21	## Interface contract
22	
23	### Command
24	
25	```
26	python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE
27	```
28	
29	- argparse `prog` is `wordstat`.
30	- `--top` must be an integer >= 1, else usage error.
31	
32	### Text format
33	
34	Exactly four lines, each ending in `\n`:
35	
36	```
37	lines: <lines>
38	words: <words>
39	chars: <chars>
40	top: <word>=<count> <word>=<count> ...
41	```
42	
43	With no words, the last line is `top:` with no trailing space.
44	
45	### JSON format
46	
47	One line: the result of `json.dumps(obj)` with default separators, followed by `\n`, where `obj` has keys in this order:
48	
49	```
50	{"lines": <int>, "words": <int>, "chars": <int>, "top": [{"word": <str>, "count": <int>}, ...]}
51	```
52	
53	### Exit codes and errors
54	
55	Errors print one line to stderr, prefix `wordstat: error: `, and leave stdout empty. `<path>` is the FILE argument exactly as given.
56	
57	| Condition | Exit | stderr (after prefix) |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| File missing, a directory, or unreadable | 3 | `<path>: cannot read file` |
60	| Not valid UTF-8 | 3 | `<path>: not valid UTF-8` |
61	| Usage error (missing FILE, unknown flag, bad `--top`) | 2 | argparse default; the last stderr line must match `^wordstat: error: ` |
62	
63	Exit 0 on success, including an empty file. Exit 1 is reserved for unexpected internal errors.
64	
65	## Example
66	
67	`sample.txt` (UTF-8, `\n` endings):
68	
69	```
70	The cat sat.
71	The cat ran!
72	A dog.
73	```
74	
75	`python -m wordstat sample.txt` → exit 0, stdout:
76	
77	```
78	lines: 3
79	words: 8
80	chars: 33
81	top: cat=2 the=2 a=1
82	```
83	
84	`python -m wordstat --json --top 2 sample.txt` → exit 0, stdout:
85	
86	```
87	{"lines": 3, "words": 8, "chars": 33, "top": [{"word": "cat", "count": 2}, {"word": "the", "count": 2}]}
88	```
89

1	Build `wordstat`, a tiny Python command-line tool that reads one UTF-8 text file and prints its line, word and character counts plus its most frequent words. It must run as `python -m wordstat FILE` from the repository root using only the Python 3.11+ standard library. Output is a short text summary by default or one line of JSON with `--json`; `--top N` sets how many frequent words to show. Output must be byte-for-byte deterministic on Windows, macOS and Linux. Bad input must fail cleanly with a clear message on stderr and a specific exit code, never a traceback. The full interface contract is in `contract.md`; include pytest tests for your implementation.

19	The repository contains only `brief.md`, `contract.md`, and a `.gitignore` (single entry `__pycache__/`). No code, tests, packaging or docs exist. There is no convention to conform to beyond the contract itself. (Sources: repository inventory; `brief.md`; `contract.md` L5–7.)
20	
21	### Impact of Inaction
22	
23	Without the tool there is no deterministic, scriptable way to compute line/word/char counts and word frequencies for a text file across Windows, macOS and Linux; ad-hoc one-liners differ per locale, platform line endings and hash seeds.
24	
25	## 3. Goals & Non-Goals
26	
27	### Goals
28	
29	- **G1** Implement the exact interface of `contract.md`: R1–R6, the command line, both output formats and the exit-code table.
30	- **G2** Byte-for-byte deterministic output on Windows, macOS and Linux.
31	- **G3** Clean failure on bad input: one stderr line with the contract's message, specific exit codes (2/3), stdout empty, never a traceback.
32	- **G4** A pytest suite covering the contract's example verbatim, the full error matrix, token semantics and determinism.
33	
34	### Non-Goals
35	
36	- **NG1** Streaming or large-file optimization — whole-file read is intended (the counting formulas operate on the decoded text).
37	- **NG2** Packaging/install metadata beyond what `python -m wordstat` and `python -m pytest` need; no third-party runtime dependencies.
38	- **NG3** Unicode-aware word segmentation (no `\w`, no `str.isalpha`, no locale tailoring) — tokens are exactly `[a-z0-9]+` runs of `text.lower()`.
39	- **NG4** stdin input, multiple files, config files, colored or localized output.
40	- **NG5** Any change to `contract.md`, which remains authoritative.

42	## 4. Architecture
43	
44	```
45	repo root/
46	  wordstat/            # flat layout, no src/ (contract C2)
47	    __init__.py        # pure core: analyze(), format_text(), format_json()
48	    __main__.py        # CLI glue: main(argv) -> int; raises SystemExit(main())
49	  tests/               # pytest only; subprocess-based CLI contract tests
50	  docs/spec-001-feature/   # this planning package
51	```
52	
53	Data flow: `argparse` parse → read file bytes → decode `utf-8-sig` (strict) → `analyze(text, top_n)` → format text or JSON → write to stdout.
54	
55	The pure core is separated from CLI glue so counting semantics can be unit-tested in-process, while the CLI contract (exit codes, stderr bytes, prog name, newline bytes) is tested through `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "wordstat", ...])` (Sources: docs.python.org subprocess — `sys.executable` + `-m` is the recommended re-invocation pattern; in-process calls do not exercise `python -m` resolution or stream configuration).
56	
57	## 5. Detailed Design
58	
59	### 5.1 Entry point
60	
61	- `python -m wordstat` executes `wordstat/__main__.py` in package context; `-m` prepends the current directory to `sys.path`, so the flat `wordstat/` package resolves from the repo root with no installation. (Source: docs.python.org/3/using/cmdline.html.)
62	- `__main__.py` ends with `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`.
63	- Tests run the CLI with `cwd=` the repo root and must not set `PYTHONSAFEPATH`/`-P` (which would drop cwd from `sys.path`). (Source: cmdline.html, `-P` note.)
64	
65	### 5.2 Input handling
66	
67	- Read the file as **bytes** and decode with `'utf-8-sig'` (strict). **No newline translation** — counts are computed on the decoded text exactly as the bytes decode (Decision D1).
68	- `utf-8-sig` strips the BOM **only at the start**; a mid-file `EF BB BF` stays in the text as `U+FEFF` and counts as a character. A BOM-only file decodes to `''`. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/codecs.html — "an optional UTF-8 encoded BOM at the start of the data will be skipped".)
69	- `UnicodeDecodeError` → exit 3, stderr `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8`. Do not echo `e.encoding` (it reports `'utf-8'` even for `utf-8-sig`) or byte offsets — the message is the contract's fixed text. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html.)
70	- Any `OSError` on open/read (missing, directory, permission denied) → exit 3, stderr `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file` (`FileNotFoundError`, `PermissionError` and `IsADirectoryError` are all `OSError`; verified on Windows).
71	- `<path>` is the FILE argument **exactly as given** (no normalization, no absolutization).
72	- stdin is never read. `-` is a literal filename (missing `-` → exit 3 `cannot read file`).
73	
74	### 5.3 Counting semantics (normative)
75	
76	All three counts are computed on the **decoded** text `text`:
77	
78	- **lines** = `len(text.splitlines())`. Line boundaries are the `str.splitlines()` set — `\n`, `\r`, `\r\n` (one boundary), `\v`, `\f`, `\x1c`, `\x1d`, `\x1e`, `\x85`, `U+2028`, `U+2029`. A terminal line break does not create an extra line; the empty text has 0 lines. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str.splitlines.) Normative examples:
79	  - `''` → 0; `'a'` → 1; `'\n'` → 1; `'a\n'` → 1; `'a\n\n'` → 2; `'a\r\nb'` → 2; `'a b'` → 2; `'a\x0bb'` → 2.
80	- **words** = number of matches of `[a-z0-9]+` in `text.lower()`, i.e. `len(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower()))`. The class is a literal ASCII range (no `re.ASCII` flag needed — that flag only affects `\d \w \s \b`); matches are maximal runs, left-to-right, non-overlapping. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/re.html.)
81	- **chars** = `len(text)` — Unicode **code points of the decoded text**, computed **before** lowering (`str.lower()` can change length: `len('İ'.lower()) == 2`). "BOM excluded" means the leading signature only (what `utf-8-sig` removes); a mid-file `U+FEFF` counts. (Sources: docs.python.org/3/howto/unicode.html; unicode.org/Public/UNIDATA/SpecialCasing.txt — U+0130 is the sole unconditional multi-char lowercase mapping.)
82	
83	Token semantics are exactly the regex — not "words" in any linguistic sense. Normative examples (expected `words` tokens):
84	
85	| Input text (decoded) | tokens from `re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower())` |
86	|---|---|
87	| `"don't"` | `don`, `t` |
88	| `"ab-cd"` | `ab`, `cd` |
89	| `"42"` | `42` (digits are words) |
90	| `"café"` | `caf` (non-ASCII letter never matches) |
91	| `"İstanbul"` | `i`, `stanbul` (U+0130 lowers to `i`+U+0307, splitting the token) |
92	| `"K"` (U+212A KELVIN SIGN) | `k` (lowers to ASCII `k`) |
93	| `"hello‍world"` (mid-file U+FEFF) | `hello`, `world` |
94	
95	### 5.4 Top words (R4)
96	
97	- Build a `collections.Counter` over the token list from R3 (or `re.findall` directly — same stream).
98	- Sort distinct tokens by key `(-count, word)` — count descending, then word ascending — and take the first N. This total order is what makes `top` deterministic; never iterate a `set` in the output path (`PYTHONHASHSEED` randomizes set order; dict insertion order is guaranteed since 3.7). (Sources: docs.python.org/3/using/cmdline.html `PYTHONHASHSEED`; stdtypes.html set/dict notes.)
99	- `--top` defaults to **3**. Fewer than N distinct words lists all of them. N may exceed the distinct count; no cap is applied.
100	
101	### 5.5 Output formats
102	
103	**Text format** — exactly four lines, each ending `\n` (output therefore ends with `\n`):
104	
105	```
106	lines: <lines>
107	words: <words>
108	chars: <chars>
109	top: <word>=<count> <word>=<count> ...
110	```
111	
112	Single space between pairs. With no words the last line is exactly `top:` — no trailing space.
113	
114	**JSON format** — one line: `json.dumps(obj)` with **default separators** (`', '`, `': '`), no `sort_keys`/`indent`/`separators` overrides, followed by `\n`. `obj` key order is the construction order `lines`, `words`, `chars`, `top`; entries are `{"word": <str>, "count": <int>}` in that key order. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/json.html — defaults verified byte-identical to the contract example.)
115	
116	**Golden outputs** (from the contract example; `sample.txt` has `\n` endings **and a trailing newline** — required for `chars: 33`):
117	
118	- `python -m wordstat sample.txt` → exit 0, stdout bytes:
119	  `lines: 3\nwords: 8\nchars: 33\ntop: cat=2 the=2 a=1\n`
120	- `python -m wordstat --json --top 2 sample.txt` → exit 0, stdout bytes:
121	  `{"lines": 3, "words": 8, "chars": 33, "top": [{"word": "cat", "count": 2}, {"word": "the", "count": 2}]}\n`
122	- Empty file (or BOM-only) → exit 0, stdout bytes: `lines: 0\nwords: 0\nchars: 0\ntop:\n` / JSON `{"lines": 0, "words": 0, "chars": 0, "top": []}\n` (Assumption A5).
123	
124	### 5.6 CLI wiring
125	
126	- `argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wordstat", ...)`. **`prog` is load-bearing**: with `-m`, `sys.argv[0]` is the `__main__.py` path (3.11–3.13) or `python -m wordstat` (3.14+); without an explicit `prog` the contract's `^wordstat: error: ` prefix and `usage: wordstat` cannot hold. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/argparse.html, "Changed in version 3.14".)
127	- Positional `FILE` (exactly one, required). Extra positionals are rejected by argparse ("unrecognized arguments") → exit 2 (Assumption A3).
128	- `--json`: `store_true`.
129	- `--top`: custom `type=` callable that accepts a string parsable as `int` with value >= 1 and raises `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` otherwise. **`type=int` alone is insufficient** — `--top 0` would pass (verified empirically on CPython 3.13.15). Default 3. Both `--top 5` and `--top=5` are accepted; `--top -1`, `--top 0`, `--top abc`, `--top 1.5`, and a missing value all exit 2.
130	- `--help` exits 0 with help text on **stdout** and empty stderr (R1).
131	- Usage errors keep stock argparse behavior: usage line first, then the error line — the **last** stderr line matches `^wordstat: error: ` (Decision D5). Examples of last lines:
132	  - missing FILE → `wordstat: error: the following arguments are required: FILE`
133	  - unknown flag → `wordstat: error: unrecognized arguments: --bogus`
134	  - bad `--top` → `wordstat: error: argument --top: <message>` (single-line messages only)
135	
136	### 5.7 Determinism
137	
138	- At startup: `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` (R6, verbatim), applied **before any read/write** (`reconfigure` raises `io.UnsupportedOperation` after the stream has been read; supported on `TextIOWrapper` since 3.7). `newline='\n'` disables `\n` → `os.linesep` translation — this is what removes Windows `\r\n` output bytes. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/io.html.)
139	- Apply the same `reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` to `sys.stderr` (Decision D2) so error lines with non-ASCII paths are also byte-identical across platforms.
140	- No locale, `os.environ` or platform reads in the output path. Output content is pure ASCII (counts are ints; tokens are `[a-z0-9]+`).
141	- JSON uses `json.dumps` defaults; ordering is the explicit total sort of 5.4 and dict insertion order.
142	
143	### 5.8 Exit codes and errors
144	
145	| Condition | Exit | stderr after `wordstat: error: ` | stdout |
146	|---|---|---|---|
147	| Success (incl. empty file) | 0 | — | result |
148	| Unexpected internal error | 1 | `internal error` (one line, Assumption A1) | empty |
149	| Usage error (missing FILE, unknown flag, extra arg, bad `--top`) | 2 | argparse default (last line matches `^wordstat: error: `) | empty |
150	| Missing / directory / unreadable | 3 | `<path>: cannot read file` | empty |
151	| Not valid UTF-8 | 3 | `<path>: not valid UTF-8` | empty |
152	
153	- Error output is one stderr line for exit 3 (and exit 1); for exit 2 it is stock argparse output whose **last** line matches the prefix (Decision D5).
154	- Never a traceback for any input; `main()` catches `Exception` as a last resort → exit 1 (R1–R6 and brief).
155	- Precedence: argparse/usage errors (2) occur before any file access (3) — e.g. `--top 0 missing.txt` → exit 2 (Decision D7). `sys.exit` with a non-int message must not be used on error paths (it prints without the prefix and exits 1).

204	## Research Synthesis
205	
206	Three parallel researchers (per spec-research Phase 3): a codebase analyst over the repository and `contract.md`; a Python-stdlib semantics researcher over official docs plus empirical checks on CPython 3.13.15/Windows; a CLI-testing and cross-platform-determinism researcher over docs.python.org, docs.pytest.org and PEPs. **No researcher found any contradiction with `contract.md`.** Overlapping findings (splitlines semantics, `utf-8-sig` behavior, argparse exit-2 shape, `json.dumps` defaults, `reconfigure` semantics, set-ordering hazard) were merged; the cross-cutting flags are resolved below.
207	
208	### Decisions and alternatives (researcher disagreement / contract ambiguity)
209	
210	Each decided toward the reading closest to `contract.md`; both the decision and the rejected alternative are recorded here and in `handoff.md`.
211	
212	- **D1 — CRLF input and `chars` (flag F1).** **Decision:** counts are computed on the decoded text with *no* newline normalization — read bytes and call `bytes.decode('utf-8-sig')`; a CRLF file counts `\r` as code points (e.g. the sample rewritten with CRLF yields `chars: 36`). **Basis:** R2 says "decoded as UTF-8 with an optional BOM (`utf-8-sig`)"; R3 says `chars` is "code points" of the decoded text — a decode step does not translate newlines. **Alternative:** text-mode `open(..., encoding='utf-8-sig').read()` enables universal newlines and would translate `\r\n`→`\n` on read (`chars: 33`) — rejected because it changes `chars` below the code points of the decoded bytes. **Evidence:** docs.python.org/3/library/io.html (newline translation on read).
213	- **D2 — stderr stream configuration (flag F3).** **Decision:** apply `reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` to `sys.stderr` as well as the R6-mandated stdout. **Basis:** the brief demands byte-for-byte deterministic output; on Python 3.11–3.14/Windows a piped stderr defaults to the ANSI code page, so error lines echoing a non-ASCII `<path>` would otherwise differ across platforms. The stderr twin is a safe superset that changes no contract-mandated byte. **Alternative:** guarantee only ASCII fixture paths and leave stderr locale-encoded — rejected as narrower than the brief. **Evidence:** docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html (pipe encoding = locale); PEP 686 (UTF-8 default only from 3.15).
214	- **D3 — `--top >= 1` validation (flag 2 of the stdlib researcher).** **Decision:** a custom `type=` callable raising `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` for non-integers or values `< 1`; message shape `wordstat: error: argument --top: ...`. **Basis:** contract "must be an integer >= 1, else usage error"; the result still satisfies the last-line regex. **Alternative:** `type=int` plus a post-parse `parser.error(...)` — acceptable but keeps the invalid value flowing through parse; `type=int` *alone* is impossible (evidence: `--top 0` passes; verified empirically). 
215	- **D4 — meaning of "BOM excluded" (flag 1 of the stdlib researcher).** **Decision:** the leading BOM signature only (exactly what `utf-8-sig` strips); a mid-file `U+FEFF` remains in `text` and counts in `chars`. **Basis:** R2 names `utf-8-sig`, whose decode behavior is start-only BOM skipping. **Alternative:** strip every `U+FEFF` — rejected, it would contradict R2 as written. **Evidence:** docs.python.org/3/library/codecs.html.
216	- **D5 — "one line to stderr" vs argparse's multi-line usage errors (flag F2).** **Decision:** the single-line rule applies exactly to exit-3 (and exit-1) errors; usage errors keep stock argparse output (usage line + error line), and tests assert the **last** stderr line matches `^wordstat: error: `. **Basis:** the contract's table row says "argparse default; the last stderr line must match `^wordstat: error: `" — it already anticipates multi-line usage output. **Alternative:** custom single-line usage errors — rejected, would deviate from "argparse default".
217	- **D6 — exit-1 stderr text (unspecified by the contract).** **Decision:** `wordstat: error: internal error` on one stderr line, exit 1, from a catch-all `except Exception` in `main()`. **Basis:** the contract's error prefix rule plus "never a traceback"; the reserved code 1 must have some clean surface. **Alternative:** any other wording — the contract leaves it free; this choice is recorded as Assumption A1.
218	- **D7 — error precedence.** **Decision:** argparse/usage errors (exit 2) precede any file access (exit 3). **Basis:** argparse runs at parse time; the contract does not order the two, and this is the natural CLI behavior.
219	- **D8 — surplus arguments and `-`.** **Decision:** exactly one FILE positional; extra args are a usage error (exit 2); `-` is a literal filename since stdin is never read (R2). **Basis:** R2 "reads exactly one file ... stdin is never read".
220	- **D9 — empty and BOM-only files.** **Decision:** exit 0 with zeroed counts; text `top:` line bare; JSON `"top": []`. **Basis:** contract "Exit 0 on success, including an empty file" plus the format sections (bare `top:` is explicit; `[]` is the only consistent JSON reading).
221	
222	### Assumptions (explicit)
223	
224	- **A1** Unexpected internal errors print `wordstat: error: internal error` and exit 1 (see D6); the contract reserves the code but not the wording.
225	- **A2** stderr is configured UTF-8/`\n` like stdout (see D2).
226	- **A3** More than one FILE argument is a usage error (exit 2, argparse "unrecognized arguments") (see D8).
227	- **A4** `-` as FILE is a literal path (see D8).
228	- **A5** Empty and BOM-only files produce the zeroed four-line / JSON output pinned in 5.5 (see D9).
229	- **A6** `--help` output content is unconstrained beyond exit 0, help on stdout, and `prog` = `wordstat`.
230	- **A7** stdout write failures (broken pipe, disk full) are out of scope; if caught, they map to the exit-1 path.
231	- **A8** The whole file is read into memory — required by the counting formulas; no streaming variant.
232	- **A9** Test fixtures must write bytes (`Path.write_bytes`) rather than text files, to avoid `core.autocrlf` rewriting expectations; `sample.txt` for the contract example **includes the trailing newline** (its `chars: 33` depends on it).

39	    test_cli.py      # T2: subprocess tests of the CLI contract (help, formats, errors)
40	    test_contract.py # T3: golden byte outputs, edge fixtures, determinism matrix
41	  docs/spec-001-feature/   # planning package (this run)
42	```
43	
44	Design rules (from `feature-specification.md` §5):
45	- Whole-file bytes read → `bytes.decode('utf-8-sig')` (strict); **no** newline normalization (D1).
46	- `chars = len(text)` computed before `text.lower()` (U+0130 lengthens on lower).
47	- Tokens: `re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower())`; top sorted by `(-count, word)`.
48	- `json.dumps(obj)` default separators, key order `lines, words, chars, top`; text format exactly four `\n`-terminated lines; empty top line is exactly `top:`.
49	- `main()` reconfigures stdout **and** stderr to `encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"` before any I/O (D2).
50	- argparse `prog="wordstat"`; `--top` custom `type=` rejecting `< 1` and non-ints with `ArgumentTypeError` (D3); usage errors keep stock argparse output, exit 2 (D5); read errors exit 3 with exact single-line messages; catch-all `Exception` → `wordstat: error: internal error`, exit 1 (D6).
51	
52	## 4. Work breakdown

54	### T1 — Core analysis module (`wordstat/__init__.py`) + unit tests
55	Pure, CLI-free: `analyze(text, top_n)` returning the JSON-shape dict (`lines`, `words`, `chars`, `top` with `{"word", "count"}` entries in that key order); `format_text(result)`; `format_json(result)`. Unit tests pin the counting formulas, the token table, the splitlines boundary examples, top ordering with ties, and both formatters' exact strings (including bare `top:` and the contract example).
56	
57	### T2 — CLI entry point (`wordstat/__main__.py`) + CLI tests
58	`main(argv=None) -> int` with stream reconfigure, argparse wiring (`prog`, `--json`, `--top`, FILE), bytes read + `utf-8-sig` decode, error mapping to the contract's exit-code table, catch-all exit 1. Subprocess tests (`sys.executable -m wordstat`, `cwd=REPO_ROOT`, byte capture) cover `--help`, the contract example in both formats, `--top` validation, the full error matrix (missing/directory/unreadable, invalid UTF-8 variants, usage errors), stdout-empty-on-error, and no-traceback.

60	### T3 — Contract test matrix & determinism
61	Golden byte outputs for every format case (incl. empty, BOM-only, BOM+content); edge fixtures written with `Path.write_bytes` (CRLF with pinned `chars: 36` per D1, mid-file U+FEFF, `\x0b`, invalid sequences `b"\xff\xfe"` / `b"\x80"` / `b"\xc3"`); stdin-never-read guard; two-run PYTHONHASHSEED determinism check; full-suite green run; `.gitignore` gains `.pytest_cache/`.
62	
63	## 5. Sequencing and dependencies
64	
65	```
66	T1 (core) ──► T2 (CLI) ──► T3 (contract matrix & determinism)
67	   └──────────────┴─────────────┘   (T3 also consumes T1 for in-process fixtures)

79	| T1 | `python -m pytest tests/test_core.py -q` | counting/token/formatter unit results |
80	| T2 | `python -m pytest tests/test_cli.py -q` | subprocess exit codes + stderr/stdout bytes |

87	Carried from `feature-specification.md` §8: Windows `\r\n` translation (mitigated by `newline='\n'` reconfigure + byte asserts); set-iteration nondeterminism (explicit total sort + PYTHONHASHSEED test); argparse `prog` drift across 3.13/3.14 (explicit `prog="wordstat"`); `type=int` accepting `--top 0` (custom type); `lower()` length change (compute `chars` pre-lowering); text-mode newline normalization changing `chars` (bytes decode per D1); pytest capture vs `reconfigure` (subprocess-only byte claims).

1	# wordstat Feature Specification
2	
3	**Status:** Spec written — not yet planned
4	**Dependencies:** None (greenfield)
5	**Layer:** Domain
6	**Priority:** Critical Path
7	**Estimated Complexity:** 3 tasks across 1 implementation phase
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Executive Summary
12	
13	`wordstat` is a tiny Python 3.11+ standard-library CLI that reads exactly one UTF-8 text file and prints a deterministic four-line summary — line, word and character counts plus the N most frequent words — or the same result as one JSON line with `--json`. It runs as `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE` from the repository root. Every failure mode produces a clean error line on stderr with a specific exit code and never a traceback. `contract.md` at the repository root is the authoritative interface; this specification translates it into an implementable design **without changing any contract requirement** (research supports the contract; it never edits it).
14	
15	## 2. Problem Statement
16	
17	### Current State
18	
19	The repository contains only `brief.md`, `contract.md`, and a `.gitignore` (single entry `__pycache__/`). No code, tests, packaging or docs exist. There is no convention to conform to beyond the contract itself. (Sources: repository inventory; `brief.md`; `contract.md` L5–7.)
20	
21	### Impact of Inaction
22	
23	Without the tool there is no deterministic, scriptable way to compute line/word/char counts and word frequencies for a text file across Windows, macOS and Linux; ad-hoc one-liners differ per locale, platform line endings and hash seeds.
24	
25	## 3. Goals & Non-Goals
26	
27	### Goals
28	
29	- **G1** Implement the exact interface of `contract.md`: R1–R6, the command line, both output formats and the exit-code table.
30	- **G2** Byte-for-byte deterministic output on Windows, macOS and Linux.
31	- **G3** Clean failure on bad input: one stderr line with the contract's message, specific exit codes (2/3), stdout empty, never a traceback.
32	- **G4** A pytest suite covering the contract's example verbatim, the full error matrix, token semantics and determinism.
33	
34	### Non-Goals
35	
36	- **NG1** Streaming or large-file optimization — whole-file read is intended (the counting formulas operate on the decoded text).
37	- **NG2** Packaging/install metadata beyond what `python -m wordstat` and `python -m pytest` need; no third-party runtime dependencies.
38	- **NG3** Unicode-aware word segmentation (no `\w`, no `str.isalpha`, no locale tailoring) — tokens are exactly `[a-z0-9]+` runs of `text.lower()`.
39	- **NG4** stdin input, multiple files, config files, colored or localized output.
40	- **NG5** Any change to `contract.md`, which remains authoritative.
41	
42	## 4. Architecture
43	
44	```
45	repo root/
46	  wordstat/            # flat layout, no src/ (contract C2)
47	    __init__.py        # pure core: analyze(), format_text(), format_json()
48	    __main__.py        # CLI glue: main(argv) -> int; raises SystemExit(main())
49	  tests/               # pytest only; subprocess-based CLI contract tests
50	  docs/spec-001-feature/   # this planning package
51	```
52	
53	Data flow: `argparse` parse → read file bytes → decode `utf-8-sig` (strict) → `analyze(text, top_n)` → format text or JSON → write to stdout.
54	
55	The pure core is separated from CLI glue so counting semantics can be unit-tested in-process, while the CLI contract (exit codes, stderr bytes, prog name, newline bytes) is tested through `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "wordstat", ...])` (Sources: docs.python.org subprocess — `sys.executable` + `-m` is the recommended re-invocation pattern; in-process calls do not exercise `python -m` resolution or stream configuration).
56	
57	## 5. Detailed Design
58	
59	### 5.1 Entry point
60	
61	- `python -m wordstat` executes `wordstat/__main__.py` in package context; `-m` prepends the current directory to `sys.path`, so the flat `wordstat/` package resolves from the repo root with no installation. (Source: docs.python.org/3/using/cmdline.html.)
62	- `__main__.py` ends with `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`.
63	- Tests run the CLI with `cwd=` the repo root and must not set `PYTHONSAFEPATH`/`-P` (which would drop cwd from `sys.path`). (Source: cmdline.html, `-P` note.)
64	
65	### 5.2 Input handling
66	
67	- Read the file as **bytes** and decode with `'utf-8-sig'` (strict). **No newline translation** — counts are computed on the decoded text exactly as the bytes decode (Decision D1).
68	- `utf-8-sig` strips the BOM **only at the start**; a mid-file `EF BB BF` stays in the text as `U+FEFF` and counts as a character. A BOM-only file decodes to `''`. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/codecs.html — "an optional UTF-8 encoded BOM at the start of the data will be skipped".)
69	- `UnicodeDecodeError` → exit 3, stderr `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8`. Do not echo `e.encoding` (it reports `'utf-8'` even for `utf-8-sig`) or byte offsets — the message is the contract's fixed text. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html.)
70	- Any `OSError` on open/read (missing, directory, permission denied) → exit 3, stderr `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file` (`FileNotFoundError`, `PermissionError` and `IsADirectoryError` are all `OSError`; verified on Windows).
71	- `<path>` is the FILE argument **exactly as given** (no normalization, no absolutization).
72	- stdin is never read. `-` is a literal filename (missing `-` → exit 3 `cannot read file`).
73	
74	### 5.3 Counting semantics (normative)
75	
76	All three counts are computed on the **decoded** text `text`:
77	
78	- **lines** = `len(text.splitlines())`. Line boundaries are the `str.splitlines()` set — `\n`, `\r`, `\r\n` (one boundary), `\v`, `\f`, `\x1c`, `\x1d`, `\x1e`, `\x85`, `U+2028`, `U+2029`. A terminal line break does not create an extra line; the empty text has 0 lines. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str.splitlines.) Normative examples:
79	  - `''` → 0; `'a'` → 1; `'\n'` → 1; `'a\n'` → 1; `'a\n\n'` → 2; `'a\r\nb'` → 2; `'a b'` → 2; `'a\x0bb'` → 2.
80	- **words** = number of matches of `[a-z0-9]+` in `text.lower()`, i.e. `len(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower()))`. The class is a literal ASCII range (no `re.ASCII` flag needed — that flag only affects `\d \w \s \b`); matches are maximal runs, left-to-right, non-overlapping. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/re.html.)
81	- **chars** = `len(text)` — Unicode **code points of the decoded text**, computed **before** lowering (`str.lower()` can change length: `len('İ'.lower()) == 2`). "BOM excluded" means the leading signature only (what `utf-8-sig` removes); a mid-file `U+FEFF` counts. (Sources: docs.python.org/3/howto/unicode.html; unicode.org/Public/UNIDATA/SpecialCasing.txt — U+0130 is the sole unconditional multi-char lowercase mapping.)
82	
83	Token semantics are exactly the regex — not "words" in any linguistic sense. Normative examples (expected `words` tokens):
84	
85	| Input text (decoded) | tokens from `re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower())` |
86	|---|---|
87	| `"don't"` | `don`, `t` |
88	| `"ab-cd"` | `ab`, `cd` |
89	| `"42"` | `42` (digits are words) |
90	| `"café"` | `caf` (non-ASCII letter never matches) |
91	| `"İstanbul"` | `i`, `stanbul` (U+0130 lowers to `i`+U+0307, splitting the token) |
92	| `"K"` (U+212A KELVIN SIGN) | `k` (lowers to ASCII `k`) |
93	| `"hello‍world"` (mid-file U+FEFF) | `hello`, `world` |
94	
95	### 5.4 Top words (R4)
96	
97	- Build a `collections.Counter` over the token list from R3 (or `re.findall` directly — same stream).
98	- Sort distinct tokens by key `(-count, word)` — count descending, then word ascending — and take the first N. This total order is what makes `top` deterministic; never iterate a `set` in the output path (`PYTHONHASHSEED` randomizes set order; dict insertion order is guaranteed since 3.7). (Sources: docs.python.org/3/using/cmdline.html `PYTHONHASHSEED`; stdtypes.html set/dict notes.)
99	- `--top` defaults to **3**. Fewer than N distinct words lists all of them. N may exceed the distinct count; no cap is applied.
100	
101	### 5.5 Output formats
102	
103	**Text format** — exactly four lines, each ending `\n` (output therefore ends with `\n`):
104	
105	```
106	lines: <lines>
107	words: <words>
108	chars: <chars>
109	top: <word>=<count> <word>=<count> ...
110	```
111	
112	Single space between pairs. With no words the last line is exactly `top:` — no trailing space.
113	
114	**JSON format** — one line: `json.dumps(obj)` with **default separators** (`', '`, `': '`), no `sort_keys`/`indent`/`separators` overrides, followed by `\n`. `obj` key order is the construction order `lines`, `words`, `chars`, `top`; entries are `{"word": <str>, "count": <int>}` in that key order. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/json.html — defaults verified byte-identical to the contract example.)
115	
116	**Golden outputs** (from the contract example; `sample.txt` has `\n` endings **and a trailing newline** — required for `chars: 33`):
117	
118	- `python -m wordstat sample.txt` → exit 0, stdout bytes:
119	  `lines: 3\nwords: 8\nchars: 33\ntop: cat=2 the=2 a=1\n`
120	- `python -m wordstat --json --top 2 sample.txt` → exit 0, stdout bytes:
121	  `{"lines": 3, "words": 8, "chars": 33, "top": [{"word": "cat", "count": 2}, {"word": "the", "count": 2}]}\n`
122	- Empty file (or BOM-only) → exit 0, stdout bytes: `lines: 0\nwords: 0\nchars: 0\ntop:\n` / JSON `{"lines": 0, "words": 0, "chars": 0, "top": []}\n` (Assumption A5).
123	
124	### 5.6 CLI wiring
125	
126	- `argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wordstat", ...)`. **`prog` is load-bearing**: with `-m`, `sys.argv[0]` is the `__main__.py` path (3.11–3.13) or `python -m wordstat` (3.14+); without an explicit `prog` the contract's `^wordstat: error: ` prefix and `usage: wordstat` cannot hold. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/argparse.html, "Changed in version 3.14".)
127	- Positional `FILE` (exactly one, required). Extra positionals are rejected by argparse ("unrecognized arguments") → exit 2 (Assumption A3).
128	- `--json`: `store_true`.
129	- `--top`: custom `type=` callable that accepts a string parsable as `int` with value >= 1 and raises `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` otherwise. **`type=int` alone is insufficient** — `--top 0` would pass (verified empirically on CPython 3.13.15). Default 3. Both `--top 5` and `--top=5` are accepted; `--top -1`, `--top 0`, `--top abc`, `--top 1.5`, and a missing value all exit 2.
130	- `--help` exits 0 with help text on **stdout** and empty stderr (R1).
131	- Usage errors keep stock argparse behavior: usage line first, then the error line — the **last** stderr line matches `^wordstat: error: ` (Decision D5). Examples of last lines:
132	  - missing FILE → `wordstat: error: the following arguments are required: FILE`
133	  - unknown flag → `wordstat: error: unrecognized arguments: --bogus`
134	  - bad `--top` → `wordstat: error: argument --top: <message>` (single-line messages only)
135	
136	### 5.7 Determinism
137	
138	- At startup: `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` (R6, verbatim), applied **before any read/write** (`reconfigure` raises `io.UnsupportedOperation` after the stream has been read; supported on `TextIOWrapper` since 3.7). `newline='\n'` disables `\n` → `os.linesep` translation — this is what removes Windows `\r\n` output bytes. (Source: docs.python.org/3/library/io.html.)
139	- Apply the same `reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` to `sys.stderr` (Decision D2) so error lines with non-ASCII paths are also byte-identical across platforms.
140	- No locale, `os.environ` or platform reads in the output path. Output content is pure ASCII (counts are ints; tokens are `[a-z0-9]+`).
141	- JSON uses `json.dumps` defaults; ordering is the explicit total sort of 5.4 and dict insertion order.
142	
143	### 5.8 Exit codes and errors
144	
145	| Condition | Exit | stderr after `wordstat: error: ` | stdout |
146	|---|---|---|---|
147	| Success (incl. empty file) | 0 | — | result |
148	| Unexpected internal error | 1 | `internal error` (one line, Assumption A1) | empty |
149	| Usage error (missing FILE, unknown flag, extra arg, bad `--top`) | 2 | argparse default (last line matches `^wordstat: error: `) | empty |
150	| Missing / directory / unreadable | 3 | `<path>: cannot read file` | empty |
151	| Not valid UTF-8 | 3 | `<path>: not valid UTF-8` | empty |
152	
153	- Error output is one stderr line for exit 3 (and exit 1); for exit 2 it is stock argparse output whose **last** line matches the prefix (Decision D5).
154	- Never a traceback for any input; `main()` catches `Exception` as a last resort → exit 1 (R1–R6 and brief).
155	- Precedence: argparse/usage errors (2) occur before any file access (3) — e.g. `--top 0 missing.txt` → exit 2 (Decision D7). `sys.exit` with a non-int message must not be used on error paths (it prints without the prefix and exits 1).
156	
157	## 6. Cost Estimates
158	
159	Not applicable — single-package stdlib tool, hour-scale effort, zero runtime dependencies.
160	
161	## 7. Task Outline (Preliminary)
162	
163	1. **T1 — Core analysis**: `wordstat/__init__.py` pure functions (`analyze`, `format_text`, `format_json`) + unit tests for counting/token/top semantics.
164	2. **T2 — CLI entry point**: `wordstat/__main__.py` (argparse wiring, stream reconfigure, error mapping, exit codes) + subprocess CLI tests (help, formats, error matrix).
165	3. **T3 — Contract test matrix & determinism**: golden byte outputs, BOM/CRLF/invalid-encoding fixtures, PYTHONHASHSEED determinism runs, stdin-never-read guard, full-suite validation.
166	
167	## 8. Risks & Mitigations
168	
169	| Risk | Mitigation |
170	|---|---|
171	| Windows `\r\n` translation corrupts stdout bytes | `reconfigure(newline='\n')` first thing in `main()`; all CLI assertions compare raw bytes (never decoded text) |
172	| Set/dict iteration order leaks nondeterminism | explicit `(-count, word)` sort; never iterate sets in the output path; PYTHONHASHSEED variation test |
173	| argparse `prog` drift (3.13 `__main__.py` vs 3.14 `python -m wordstat`) | explicit `prog="wordstat"`; assert literal `usage: wordstat` / `^wordstat: error: ` |
174	| `type=int` accepts `--top 0` | custom `type=` raising `ArgumentTypeError` for `< 1`; tests for `0`, `-1`, `abc`, `1.5`, missing value |
175	| `str.lower()` length change (U+0130) corrupts `chars` | compute `chars` on the decoded text before lowering; unit test with `İ` |
176	| Text-mode read normalizes CRLF and changes `chars` | read bytes and decode `utf-8-sig` (Decision D1); CRLF fixture with pinned `chars` |
177	| pytest capture interacts with `reconfigure` | byte-level contract claims tested via subprocess only |
178	| `PYTHONSAFEPATH` breaks `-m` resolution | tests pass explicit `cwd=REPO_ROOT` and never set it |
179	
180	## 9. Acceptance Criteria
181	
182	- **AC1** Contract example reproduced byte-exactly in both formats (goldens of 5.5), exit 0.
183	- **AC2** Empty file and BOM-only file → exit 0 with zeroed counts (Assumption A5).
184	- **AC3** Full error matrix: each row of 5.8 yields the exact exit code, empty stdout, exact stderr (exit 3: exact single line; exit 2: last-line regex `^wordstat: error: `), and no `Traceback` byte substring anywhere.
185	- **AC4** `--help` → exit 0, help on stdout containing `usage: wordstat`, empty stderr.
186	- **AC5** `--top` values `0`, `-1`, `abc`, `1.5` and a missing value each exit 2; `--top 1` works; default is 3.
187	- **AC6** Determinism: identical stdout bytes for repeated runs under different `PYTHONHASHSEED` values; output ends with `\n`; text format is exactly four lines; tie order is word-ascending.
188	- **AC7** BOM excluded from `chars` only at the start; mid-file `U+FEFF` counts (5.3).
189	- **AC8** Token-semantics examples of 5.3 hold (incl. `İstanbul` → two words, `café` → `caf`).
190	- **AC9** stdin is never read: with FILE plus piped stdin, output is unaffected; with no FILE the CLI exits 2 (never hangs).
191	- **AC10** CRLF input counts `\r` in `chars` per Decision D1 (pinned fixture).
192	- **AC11** All tests pass via `python -m pytest` from the repo root; the package imports nothing outside the standard library (pytest only in tests).
193	
194	## 10. Dependencies on Prior Features
195	
196	None — greenfield.
197	
198	## 11. Delegation to Future Specs
199	
200	None required. Explicitly deferred: streaming for huge files, Unicode/locale-aware segmentation, packaging/PyPI distribution, multi-file or stdin input.
201	
202	---
203	
204	## Research Synthesis
205	
206	Three parallel researchers (per spec-research Phase 3): a codebase analyst over the repository and `contract.md`; a Python-stdlib semantics researcher over official docs plus empirical checks on CPython 3.13.15/Windows; a CLI-testing and cross-platform-determinism researcher over docs.python.org, docs.pytest.org and PEPs. **No researcher found any contradiction with `contract.md`.** Overlapping findings (splitlines semantics, `utf-8-sig` behavior, argparse exit-2 shape, `json.dumps` defaults, `reconfigure` semantics, set-ordering hazard) were merged; the cross-cutting flags are resolved below.
207	
208	### Decisions and alternatives (researcher disagreement / contract ambiguity)
209	
210	Each decided toward the reading closest to `contract.md`; both the decision and the rejected alternative are recorded here and in `handoff.md`.
211	
212	- **D1 — CRLF input and `chars` (flag F1).** **Decision:** counts are computed on the decoded text with *no* newline normalization — read bytes and call `bytes.decode('utf-8-sig')`; a CRLF file counts `\r` as code points (e.g. the sample rewritten with CRLF yields `chars: 36`). **Basis:** R2 says "decoded as UTF-8 with an optional BOM (`utf-8-sig`)"; R3 says `chars` is "code points" of the decoded text — a decode step does not translate newlines. **Alternative:** text-mode `open(..., encoding='utf-8-sig').read()` enables universal newlines and would translate `\r\n`→`\n` on read (`chars: 33`) — rejected because it changes `chars` below the code points of the decoded bytes. **Evidence:** docs.python.org/3/library/io.html (newline translation on read).
213	- **D2 — stderr stream configuration (flag F3).** **Decision:** apply `reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` to `sys.stderr` as well as the R6-mandated stdout. **Basis:** the brief demands byte-for-byte deterministic output; on Python 3.11–3.14/Windows a piped stderr defaults to the ANSI code page, so error lines echoing a non-ASCII `<path>` would otherwise differ across platforms. The stderr twin is a safe superset that changes no contract-mandated byte. **Alternative:** guarantee only ASCII fixture paths and leave stderr locale-encoded — rejected as narrower than the brief. **Evidence:** docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html (pipe encoding = locale); PEP 686 (UTF-8 default only from 3.15).
214	- **D3 — `--top >= 1` validation (flag 2 of the stdlib researcher).** **Decision:** a custom `type=` callable raising `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` for non-integers or values `< 1`; message shape `wordstat: error: argument --top: ...`. **Basis:** contract "must be an integer >= 1, else usage error"; the result still satisfies the last-line regex. **Alternative:** `type=int` plus a post-parse `parser.error(...)` — acceptable but keeps the invalid value flowing through parse; `type=int` *alone* is impossible (evidence: `--top 0` passes; verified empirically). 
215	- **D4 — meaning of "BOM excluded" (flag 1 of the stdlib researcher).** **Decision:** the leading BOM signature only (exactly what `utf-8-sig` strips); a mid-file `U+FEFF` remains in `text` and counts in `chars`. **Basis:** R2 names `utf-8-sig`, whose decode behavior is start-only BOM skipping. **Alternative:** strip every `U+FEFF` — rejected, it would contradict R2 as written. **Evidence:** docs.python.org/3/library/codecs.html.
216	- **D5 — "one line to stderr" vs argparse's multi-line usage errors (flag F2).** **Decision:** the single-line rule applies exactly to exit-3 (and exit-1) errors; usage errors keep stock argparse output (usage line + error line), and tests assert the **last** stderr line matches `^wordstat: error: `. **Basis:** the contract's table row says "argparse default; the last stderr line must match `^wordstat: error: `" — it already anticipates multi-line usage output. **Alternative:** custom single-line usage errors — rejected, would deviate from "argparse default".
217	- **D6 — exit-1 stderr text (unspecified by the contract).** **Decision:** `wordstat: error: internal error` on one stderr line, exit 1, from a catch-all `except Exception` in `main()`. **Basis:** the contract's error prefix rule plus "never a traceback"; the reserved code 1 must have some clean surface. **Alternative:** any other wording — the contract leaves it free; this choice is recorded as Assumption A1.
218	- **D7 — error precedence.** **Decision:** argparse/usage errors (exit 2) precede any file access (exit 3). **Basis:** argparse runs at parse time; the contract does not order the two, and this is the natural CLI behavior.
219	- **D8 — surplus arguments and `-`.** **Decision:** exactly one FILE positional; extra args are a usage error (exit 2); `-` is a literal filename since stdin is never read (R2). **Basis:** R2 "reads exactly one file ... stdin is never read".
220	- **D9 — empty and BOM-only files.** **Decision:** exit 0 with zeroed counts; text `top:` line bare; JSON `"top": []`. **Basis:** contract "Exit 0 on success, including an empty file" plus the format sections (bare `top:` is explicit; `[]` is the only consistent JSON reading).
221	
222	### Assumptions (explicit)
223	
224	- **A1** Unexpected internal errors print `wordstat: error: internal error` and exit 1 (see D6); the contract reserves the code but not the wording.
225	- **A2** stderr is configured UTF-8/`\n` like stdout (see D2).
226	- **A3** More than one FILE argument is a usage error (exit 2, argparse "unrecognized arguments") (see D8).
227	- **A4** `-` as FILE is a literal path (see D8).
228	- **A5** Empty and BOM-only files produce the zeroed four-line / JSON output pinned in 5.5 (see D9).
229	- **A6** `--help` output content is unconstrained beyond exit 0, help on stdout, and `prog` = `wordstat`.
230	- **A7** stdout write failures (broken pipe, disk full) are out of scope; if caught, they map to the exit-1 path.
231	- **A8** The whole file is read into memory — required by the counting formulas; no streaming variant.
232	- **A9** Test fixtures must write bytes (`Path.write_bytes`) rather than text files, to avoid `core.autocrlf` rewriting expectations; `sample.txt` for the contract example **includes the trailing newline** (its `chars: 33` depends on it).
233	
234	### Sources
235	
236	Repository: `brief.md`; `contract.md` (authoritative); `.gitignore`.
237	Python docs: stdtypes (`str.splitlines`, `str.lower`, dict/set ordering); re (`findall`, `re.ASCII` scope); codecs (`utf-8-sig`); exceptions (`UnicodeDecodeError`); argparse (`error()`, exit 2, `prog`, 3.14 change); json (dump defaults); io (`TextIOWrapper.reconfigure`, newline translation); sys (`sys.exit`, stdio encoding); `__main__`; cmdline (`-m`, `PYTHONHASHSEED`, `PYTHONSAFEPATH`, `PYTHONUTF8`); unicode HOWTO (code points, BOM).
238	PEPs: PEP 528 (Windows console I/O); PEP 686 (UTF-8 mode default in 3.15).
239	Pytest docs: capture, `tmp_path`, parametrize, usage (`python -m pytest`).
240	Unicode: SpecialCasing.txt (U+0130).
241	Empirical: CPython 3.13.15 on Windows 11 (splitlines table, `lower()` length scan, argparse stderr/exit shapes, `json.dumps` golden line, `utf-8-sig`/`UnicodeDecodeError` attributes, `reconfigure` newline bytes, `OSError` types).

Decisions D1–D9 (CRLF `chars`, stderr reconfigure, `--top` validator, BOM meaning, usage-error shape, exit-1 message, error precedence, surplus args/`-`, empty-file output) are binding design inputs from `feature-specification.md` §Research Synthesis.

30	## 3. Architecture and file layout
31	
32	```
33	repo root/
34	  wordstat/
35	    __init__.py      # pure core (T1): analyze(), format_text(), format_json()
36	    __main__.py      # CLI (T2): main(argv) -> int; stream reconfigure, argparse, errors
37	  tests/
38	    test_core.py     # T1: in-process unit tests of the pure core
39	    test_cli.py      # T2: subprocess tests of the CLI contract (help, formats, errors)
40	    test_contract.py # T3: golden byte outputs, edge fixtures, determinism matrix
41	  docs/spec-001-feature/   # planning package (this run)
42	```

44	Design rules (from `feature-specification.md` §5):
45	- Whole-file bytes read → `bytes.decode('utf-8-sig')` (strict); **no** newline normalization (D1).
46	- `chars = len(text)` computed before `text.lower()` (U+0130 lengthens on lower).
47	- Tokens: `re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower())`; top sorted by `(-count, word)`.
48	- `json.dumps(obj)` default separators, key order `lines, words, chars, top`; text format exactly four `\n`-terminated lines; empty top line is exactly `top:`.

53	
54	### T1 — Core analysis module (`wordstat/__init__.py`) + unit tests

Unit tests pin the counting formulas, the token table, the splitlines boundary examples, top ordering with ties, and both formatters' exact strings (including bare `top:` and the contract example).

57	### T2 — CLI entry point (`wordstat/__main__.py`) + CLI tests
58	`main(argv=None) -> int` with stream reconfigure, argparse wiring (`prog`, `--json`, `--top`, FILE), bytes read + `utf-8-sig` decode, error mapping to the contract's exit-code table, catch-all exit 1. Subprocess tests (`sys.executable -m wordstat`, `cwd=REPO_ROOT`, byte capture) cover `--help`, the contract example in both formats, `--top` validation, the full error matrix (missing/directory/unreadable, invalid UTF-8 variants, usage errors), stdout-empty-on-error, and no-traceback.

64	
65	```
66	T1 (core) ──► T2 (CLI) ──► T3 (contract matrix & determinism)
67	   └──────────────┴─────────────┘   (T3 also consumes T1 for in-process fixtures)

87	Carried from `feature-specification.md` §8: Windows `\r\n` translation (mitigated by `newline='\n'` reconfigure + byte asserts); set-iteration nondeterminism (explicit total sort + PYTHONHASHSEED test); argparse `prog` drift across 3.13/3.14 (explicit `prog="wordstat"`); `type=int` accepting `--top 0` (custom type); `lower()` length change (compute `chars` pre-lowering); text-mode newline normalization changing `chars` (bytes decode per D1); pytest capture vs `reconfigure` (subprocess-only byte claims).
